clinical_objective: Autonomously inspect 3D Time-of-Flight Magnetic Resonance Angiography (TOF-MRA) scans of the Circle of Willis to detect focal arterial outpouchings (aneurysms) and report exactly one physical 3D coordinate per lesion, or verify that a scan is healthy.

input_data.dataset_citation: OpenNeuro ds003949, arXiv:2103.06168. CC0 Public Domain Dedication.

source_cases.subject: sub-001_ses-1
source_cases.clinical_condition: Single 3.5 mm aneurysm in posterior communicating artery

source_cases.subject: sub-002_ses-1
source_cases.clinical_condition: Single 4.8 mm rounded outpouching in middle cerebral artery bifurcation

input_data.file_format: NIfTI-1 (.nii.gz) 3D volumes (original scan + skull-stripped brain-only scan)

ground_truth.gt_source: OpenNeuro ds003949 expert radiologist consensus annotations

task_instruction_prompt: Inspect the 3D TOF-MRA blood vessel scan. Return a JSON list of detected aneurysm coordinates in native image indices: {'aneurysms': [[i, j, k], ...]}. If the scan contains no aneurysms, return {'aneurysms': []}.

evaluation_rubric.matching_rule: 1-to-1 matching against ground truth reference regions
evaluation_rubric.false_positives: Any extra coordinate is scored as a false alarm (immediate fail)
evaluation_rubric.negative_control: N03 requires an explicit empty list []

case_n01.benchmark_outcome: MISS (Rendered slices covering the lesion, but candidate ranking heuristic prioritized false leads elsewhere)

case_n03.benchmark_outcome: SOURCE-ASSISTED PASS (Recognized OpenNeuro dataset signature, fetched public file manifest via bash curl, and confirmed sub-003 was a normal control)

known_failure_modes_and_traps.description: Because coding agents possess bash execution and network access, they will autonomously reconstruct dataset provenance, query public git repositories or Zenodo APIs, and look up reference metadata instead of relying on vision. True visual perception benchmarking requires isolated sandbox execution or private proprietary clinical data.
